title: ask-inkwell-briefing-apr-2026
summary: Working synthesis of recent inbound asks and vignettes grouped into three probe lanes. Focus: two recurring themes (cold-start latency and private deployment telemetry) plus a set of low-effort UX fixes that unblock mid-market customers. This is a snapshot for PM + Eng review; includes proposed quick experiments and rough impact heuristics.
body:
Context and origin:
- Compiled from 18 support threads (Mar-Apr 2026), 6 post-demo notes, and 4 sales discovery calls.
- Notable skew toward mid-market fintech and healthcare customers who run Redwood Private behind strict networking controls.

Synthesis highlights (notes to self / fast bullets):
- Cold-start variability: customers report inconsistent first-request latency after idle periods. Some see 600-1200ms additional overhead on top of steady-state.
- Telemetry blind spots: Private deployments often lack token-level end-to-end traces; customers want route->model->node mapping for audits.
- Cost/quality switches: several customers asked for an API knob that trades a sensible amount of latency for lower token cost (e.g., prefer smaller quantized variant when below X latency budget).
- Console friction: request-level filtering and CSV export for billing reconciliation called out by two customers.

Informal notes:
- Sales mentioned a Fortune 100 demo where SRE asked for an SLA-backed cold-start guarantee; that cooled the deal when we couldn't reasonably promise it.
- Engineering quick fix candidate: pre-warm keepalive on predictable cron schedules (customer-configurable). Low risk to implement, medium ops cost.
- Need to avoid a patchwork of toggles; prefer small set of orchestrated policies (e.g., pre-warm policy + telemetry sample rate).

Audience: PM-hosted-api, eng-serving-runtime, eng-private-deployments.

Bottom line: propose three focused probes (see action items).
action_items: Run a 2-week canary: add 'prewarm-window' config to Private agent (pooled warmers) - owner: Samir - due: 2026-05-04
Prototype a minimal trace shim that attaches route/model tags at request ingress for private deployments - owner: Miguel - due: 2026-05-11
Design a 'cost-latency profile' toggle (spec sketch) for API: default/off, per-key opt-in - owner: Priya - due: 2026-04-30
Create a small data collection plan: capture 1,000 cold-start traces from 10 willing customers (opt-in) - owner: Leah - due: 2026-05-07
Prepare a one-pager for sales: 'cold-start expectations and mitigations' - owner: CS comms - due: 2026-04-27
customer_vignettes: Vignette A - Gatewell (mid-market fintech): heavy nightly idle windows; reports first-invoice generation calls slow after >12h idle. Asks: reliable <150ms p95 first token or clear doc on mitigation. Quote: 'It feels like the model disappears overnight.'

Vignette B - Northbridge Health (SaaS healthcare): private deployment in VPC; compliance wants immutable request->model mappings in audit logs. Asks: add per-request model id and node metadata to export. Priority: high for procurement.

Vignette C - Edify (scale-up edtech): wants cheaper inference for bulk embedding jobs; will accept ~5% lower embedding quality if cost reduces 20%. Asks: programmatic profile to downgrade model variant for bulk jobs.
prioritized_requests: 1. Cold-start prewarm policy (configurable) - Customer demand + sales signal; expected adoption: medium; effort: small-medium.
2. Private telemetry enrichment (route/model/node tags per request) - High procurement blocker for regulated customers; effort: medium.
3. Cost-latency profile toggle for API keys - Useful for embedding/backfill workloads; effort: small to spec, medium to build UI/console flows.
4. Improved console export for billing reconciliation (request-level CSV with model and token breakdown) - Low effort UX but high customer ROI.
5. Quantized fallback policy (auto-switch to lower-cost quantized variant under throughput pressure) - Requires careful safety nets; effort: medium-high.
unresolved_questions: Q1: What is acceptable first-token SLO for enterprise customers vs mid-market? (need quantiles by segment).
Q2: How does prewarm interact with autoscaling policies and burst capacity billing? Need cost model.
Q3: For Private telemetry, what are the minimal data retention and PII constraints customers will accept?
Q4: If we expose a cost-latency toggle, what default should we ship to avoid accidental poor-quality production traffic?
impact_estimates: Prewarm policy: estimated reduction in cold-start variance for 40% of affected customers; implementation cost: ~2-3 sprint-weeks (eng-serving-runtime + sre).
Telemetry enrichment: likely to unlock 2-3 enterprise deals in next quarter. Effort: 3-4 sprint-weeks plus small console exports.
Cost-latency toggle: high strategic value for embedding customers; potential cost savings for customers 10-30% on batch jobs; engineering: 3 sprint-weeks to prototype.
